data.narrative:
Echodyne is a Series C–stage defense and security company that has raised $224M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of three same-sector, same-stage private peers (Castelion, Stark Defence, Neros) alongside a broader set of ten defense-tech companies spanning public and private markets, including public comparables DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $224M total raised as a proxy for current value, yielding $381M. Peer-median methodology identifies three directly comparable Series C companies in Defense & Security with valuations ranging from $2.5B (Neros) to $13.0B (Castelion), with a median of $4.0B. This significant spread reflects heterogeneity in scale and market position within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $324M (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $2.2B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether Echodyne tracks closer to earlier-stage funding-based multiples or commands a premium aligned with higher-valuation peers. Key dependencies include revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and market differentiation relative to named competitors. The median estimate of $2.2B represents a 9.8x multiple on total capital deployed, substantially higher than the stage-progression method alone, suggesting peer comparables are driving valuation assumptions.
